      - text: Looking to brighten up your indoor space with Sedum japonicum 'Tokyo Sun'? Here's a simple
      - strong: Indoor Care Routine Hack
      - text: "to keep those golden leaves glowing and healthy:"
      - heading "💡 Lighting Hack:" [level=4]:
        - img "💡"
        - strong: "Lighting Hack:"
      - text: If your home lacks bright natural light, no worries! Use an affordable
      - strong: clip-on grow light
      - text: near a south- or east-facing window. This keeps the plant vibrant even in darker corners.

      - list:
        - strong: "Tip:"
        - text: Stick a wooden skewer or chopstick into the soil to check moisture. If it comes out dry, it's time to water!
        - generic: Always use pots with drainage holes to prevent soggy roots.

        - img "🌬️"
        - strong: "Humidity Hack:"
      - generic: Sedum loves dry air, so avoid placing it in bathrooms. If you’re in a humid climate, pop a small dehumidifier nearby or keep it in an air-conditioned room.
      - heading "🌡️ Temperature Hack:" [level=4]:
        - img "🌡️"
        - strong: "Temperature Hack:"
      - generic: Keep the plant cozy by avoiding drafty windows in winter. Move it closer to the center of the room to maintain a stable temperature (60–75°F).

        - img "🌱"
        - strong: "Soil & Potting Hack:"
      - text: Mix your own

        - generic: 3 parts potting soil
        - generic: 2 parts coarse sand
        - text: 1 part perlite
        - text: This ensures excellent drainage and happy roots!
      - heading "🌟 Fertilization Hack:" [level=4]:
        - img "🌟"
        - strong: "Fertilization Hack:"
      - text: In spring and summer, dilute regular succulent fertilizer to
      - strong: half-strength
      - text: . Feed it once a month for that extra glow—but skip feeding in winter to let it rest.
      - img "💡"
      - strong: "Pro Tip:"
      - text: Group your succulents together for a trendy indoor garden vibe, and they’ll help each other maintain optimal humidity!
